findings.finding: Case equal and ρ = extends are supported. All nine case loci are verbatim at the named sections: #727 header, §0, §2.3 and §4; #726 Governing Doctrine and §11.5; #533 §II; #1634 §1; #18 Introduction. #727 also names the relation in so many words ('Semantic Economy is Lee Sharks' contemporary extension and disclosure of political economy'), and its matrix calls political economy the 'disclosed parent field'. A reader of the same papers would decide the same way. The witness reading fails because the archive does not contest the field's object; it adds a substrate to it ('does not abolish political economy'). The mixed reading fails because #727 itself places its strongest sense next to an existing field (cultural political economy), so §0.10 does not apply. E531-02 ('semantic infrastructure is ontologically prior to debt-bearing economic systems') is the strongest ontological sense, and it too is stated about the field's object.

findings.fix: None to the reading. Optionally add the §0 'extension and disclosure' sentence to the case loci, since it states ρ in its own word.

summary: Equal/extends confirmed and every claim of both ledgers is composed with received quotes verbatim, but the KO misplaces #247's 'semantic economy' Overview as if it were political economy's, leaves many field claims unattributed (KO 5-7, P lede and nine items) while every archive claim carries its number, closes with an 18-sentence archive-only block, lists translation pairings that are not composed together, and alters several claims (F36 'just', F30 'can help', E467-02 disjunction, E727-12, E1666-04 scope, #122's undated count) plus an open-block question that cushions #727's canonical claim.
